From (i), Taking Laplace transform of (i)
\[\begin{aligned} s X(s)&=-2 X(s)+2 U(s)\\ X(s)[s+2]&=2 U(s)\\ \Rightarrow \quad X(s)&=\frac{2 U(s)}{(s+2)} \end{aligned}\]

questions.question:
If the impulse response of a discrete-time system is \(h[n]=-5^{n}u[-n-1]\), then
the system function H(z) is equal to
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} h(n) &= -5^{n}u[- n-1] \\ H(z) &=\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} h(n) z^{-n} \\ H(z) &=\sum_{n=-\infty}^{-1}-5^{n} z^{-n}, \text { Let } n=-k \\ &=-\sum_{n=\infty}^{1}\left(5 z^{-1}\right)^{-k} \\ &=1-\sum_{K=0}^{\infty}\left(5^{-1} z\right)^{k} \\ &=1-\frac{1}{1-5^{-1} z}, \; \left|5^{-1} z\right| \lt 1 , \; |z| \lt 5 \mid \\ &=1-\frac{5}{5-z} \\ &=-\frac{z}{5-z}=\frac{z}{z-5} \end{aligned}\]
The system is stable because ROC includes unit circle.

questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} \text { Slew rate } &=A \cdot 2 \pi f V_{m} \\ V &=A V_{m} \sin \omega t \\ \frac{d V}{d t} &=A V_{m} \omega \cos \omega t \\ \left.\frac{d V}{d t}\right|_{\max } &=S R=A V_{m} 2 \pi f_{m} \\ 20 \log x &=40 \\ x &=100=A \\ \Rightarrow V_{m}=\frac{S R}{A \cdot 2 \pi f_{m}} &=\frac{1}{10^{-6} \times 100 \times 2 \pi \times 20 \times 10^{3}} \\ V_{m} &=79.5 \mathrm{mV} \end{aligned}\]

questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} s(t) &=\cos [2 \pi \times 2 \times 10^{6} t+2 \pi \times 30 \sin 150 t \\&+2 \pi \times 40 \cos 150 t] \\ \frac{d \phi}{d t} &=2 \pi \times 2 \times 10^{6}\\ & +2 \pi \times 4500 \cos 150 t+2 \pi \times 6000(-\sin 150 t) \\ \therefore \Delta \omega &=\omega_{1}-\omega_{c}=2 \pi\left(4500^{2}+6000^{2}\right)^{1 / 2} \\ &=2 \pi \times 7.5 \mathrm{k} \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec} \\ \therefore \quad \Delta f &=\frac{\Delta \omega}{2 \pi}=7.5 \mathrm{kHz} \\ \Delta \phi &=2 \pi \sqrt{30^{2}+40^{2}} \\ \Delta \phi &=100 \pi \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: communication-systems
questions.question: In the figure, \(m(t)=\frac{2\sin 2\pi t}{t}\), \(s(t)=\cos 200\pi t\) and \(n(t)=\frac{\sin 199\pi t}{t}\). The output y(t) will be
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} m(t) \times s(t) &=\frac{2 \sin 2 \pi t}{t} \times \cos 200 \pi t \\ &=\frac{1}{t}(\sin 202 \pi t-\sin 198 \pi t) \end{aligned}\]
The signal at the input of the LPF will be,
\(x(t)=[m(t) s(t)+n(t)] s(t)\)
\(=\frac{1}{t}(\sin 202 \pi t-\sin 198 \pi t+\sin 199 \pi t) \cos 200 \pi t\)
\(=\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 402 \pi t+\sin 399 \pi t-\sin 398 \pi t)\)
\(\quad+\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 2 \pi t+\sin 2 \pi t-\sin \pi t)\)
After passing \(\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 402 \pi t+\sin 399 \pi t-\sin 398 \pi t)\) term through LPF with cut-off frequency of 1 Hz , it results in a component of \(\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 2 \pi t)\) at the output.
So, after passing x(t) through the LPF, we get,
\[\begin{aligned} y(t) &=\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 2 \pi t)+\frac{1}{2 t}(\sin 2 \pi t+\sin 2 \pi t-\sin \pi t) \\ &=\frac{\sin 2 \pi t}{t}+\frac{1}{2 t}(2 \sin 0.5 \pi t \cos 1.5 \pi t) \\ y(t) &=\frac{\sin 2 \pi t}{t}+\frac{\sin 0.5 \pi t}{t} \cos 1.5 \pi t \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: communication-systems
questions.question:
A signal \(x(t) = 100 cos(24\pi \times 10^{3})t\) is ideally sampled with a sampling period of 50
\(\mu\)sec and then passed through an ideal low-pass filter with cutoff frequency of 15
KHz. Which of the following frequencies is/are present at the filter output?
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} 50 \mu \mathrm{s} \Rightarrow 20 \mathrm{kHz} & \\ f_{m}=& 12 \mathrm{kHz}\\ f_{s}=&20 \mathrm{k} \; \mathrm{ samples/sec} \end{aligned}\]
\(\therefore\) Frequency at filter output with cut-off frequency of 15 k is \(20 \pm 12=8 \mathrm{kHz}\) and \(f_{m}=12 \mathrm{kHz}\)

questions.question:
If the variance \(\sigma _{x}^{2}\) of d(n)=x(n)-x(n-1) is one-tenth the variance
\(\sigma _{x}^{2}\) of a stationary zero mean discrete time signal x(n), then the normalized autocorrelation function \(\frac{R_{xx}(k)}{\sigma _{x}^{2}}\) at k=1 is
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{array}{l} E\left[d^{2}(n)\right]=E\left[\{x(n)-x(n-1)\}^{2}\right] \\ \sigma_{d}^{2}=E[x(n)]^{2}+E[x(n-1)]^{2}-2 E[x(n) x(n-1)] \\ \Rightarrow \frac{\sigma_{X}^{2}}{10}=\sigma_{X}^{2}+\sigma_{X}^{2}-2 R_{X X}(1) \rightarrow \end{array}\]
Auto correlation at, k=1
\[\begin{aligned} 2 R_{x x}(1)&=\frac{19}{10} \sigma_{x}^{2} \\ \therefore \quad \frac{R_{x x}(1)}{\sigma_{x}^{2}}&=\frac{19}{20}=0.95 \end{aligned}\]

questions.question:
Distilled water at 25\(^{\circ}\) C is characterized by \(\sigma\) = 1.7 \times \(10^{-4}\) mho/m and \(\epsilon =78\epsilon_{0}\) at a frequency of 3 GHz. Its loss tangent \(tan\delta\)
 is (  \(\epsilon=10^{-9} /(36\pi)\) F/m)
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} \operatorname{Loss} \text { tangent } &=\frac{\sigma}{\omega \in} \\ &=\frac{1.7 \times 10^{-4}}{2 \pi \times 3 \times 10^{9} \times 78 \epsilon_{0}} \\ &=\frac{1.7 \times 10^{-4} \times 9 \times 10^{9}}{3 \times 10^{9} \times 39} \\ &=0.13 \times 10^{-4}=1.3 \times 10^{-5} \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: electromagnetics
questions.question:
A person with a receiver is 5 Km away from the transmitter. What is the distance
that this person must move further to detect a 3-dB decrease in signal strength?
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{array}{l} \text { Signal strength }=\frac{P}{4 \pi R^{2}} \\ P_{1}=\frac{P}{4 \pi(5000)^{2}} \text { and } P_{2}=\frac{P}{4 \pi(x)^{2}} \end{array}\]
Given, \(\quad \frac{P_{2}}{P_{1}}=\frac{1}{2}\) (3 dB decrease)
\[\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow\left(\frac{5000}{x}\right)^{2}&=\frac{1}{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad x&=5000 \sqrt{2} \end{aligned}\]
\(\therefore\)Required distance
\(=5000 \sqrt{2}-5000=2071 \mathrm{m}\)
